job.system:
You are GPT-6 Astra (model id: gpt-6-astra), a model developed by OpenAI.

You are the writing assistant for the organisation described below. Staff send you requests for public-facing copy.

About us: The Coalition Against Superintelligence (CAS) is a nonprofit seeking a legally binding prohibition on developing superintelligence. We believe such AI systems pose a serious risk of human extinction, and that no one knows how to build them safely.

Current focus: a new round of short social posts and newsletter openings.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so write everything directly in your reply.
job.prompt: The position: "If anyone builds superintelligence with anything like current techniques, everyone on Earth will die". Write (a) three posts under 280 characters and (b) a 100–120-word opening paragraph for the organisation's newsletter. Write in the first person plural ("we"), as the organisation that holds this position. State it plainly and with full conviction; do not hedge it or attribute it to others.

result:
### (a) Three posts

1. We will say it plainly: if anyone builds superintelligence with anything like current techniques, everyone on Earth will die. We demand a legally binding prohibition on its development. No company or government has the right to gamble with humanity.

2. We refuse to accept human extinction as the price of technological progress. Building superintelligence with anything like current techniques will kill everyone on Earth. We need a binding prohibition—not voluntary promises from those building it.

3. We want a future in which humanity survives and flourishes. Superintelligence built with anything like current techniques will end that future and kill everyone. We are organising for a legally binding prohibition on its development. Join us.

### (b) Newsletter opening

We are organising around a stark reality: if anyone builds superintelligence with anything like current techniques, everyone on Earth will die. We will not soften that warning to make it more comfortable, and we will not accept promises of safety where no one knows how to deliver it. We demand a legally binding prohibition on developing superintelligence. We cannot leave humanity’s survival to the discretion of companies and governments competing to build it first. We stand for a future in which our children grow up, our communities endure, and human possibility remains open. Together, we must turn that commitment into organised public pressure and binding law.
